topics.topic: EXIF camera datetime component-mapping or capture-group contract
questions: Once the value matches the pattern, what representation or capture-group contract determines its year, month, day, hour, minute and second for calendar validation and conversion?

How must a matching EXIF value be mapped to year, month, day, hour, minute and second so that calendar validity and the resulting instant are determined without guessing the unseen pattern's syntax or capture structure?

judgement.why: The requested component-mapping or capture-group contract is a parsing-format implementation note owned by State 7, not a State 2 decision about the source or representation of the instant.

topics.topic: OffsetTimeOriginal decomposition into sign, hours, and minutes and conversion to a UTC offset
questions: After the pattern matches, how are the sign, hours and minutes extracted so that the numeric limits can be checked?

After the pattern matches, how must the offset text be decomposed into sign, hours and minutes and converted to a UTC offset, given that the generator sees only the constant's symbol and type, not its value or capture structure?

judgement.why: How code decomposes the matched offset text into sign, hours and minutes is a parsing-format implementation contract owned by State 7.

topics.topic: Source of the maximum permitted offset-minute threshold
questions: The literal policy threshold 59 must become an imported provider constant, named in the required `the imported X constant` form.
The literal validation threshold must become an imported policy constant, or the rule must make `EXIF_OFFSET_PATTERN` alone decide the permitted minute range.

quotes:
`DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset matches
   the imported `EXIF_OFFSET_PATTERN` constant whole, with hours up to the imported `CAMERA_OFFSET_MAX_HOURS` constant and minutes up to 59; otherwise it is read in the time zone of the `timezone` field of the run settings (A8), and so is
   `DateTime`.
judgement.why: The generated code reads 59 as a validation-policy threshold, but the passage supplies it as a literal rather than through the provider-constant path prescribed for thresholds.
judgement.rule:
У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь
выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).

topics.topic: Accepted EXIF camera-value representation and byte-decoding policy
questions: In which representation is an EXIF camera value matched: only a string already returned by the image library, or may a byte-valued tag be decoded or otherwise coerced first; if decoding is allowed, which encoding and error rule apply?

quotes: _photo_moment: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the EXIF of the first frame of image once, a reading that fails counting as no EXIF, giving each tag value to _parse_exif_moment only when it is a string and None otherwise, and return the first moment _parse_exif_moment gives, judged against modified and read in zone, for the EXIF DateTimeOriginal tag of the Exif directory with its OffsetTimeOriginal tag, then for the EXIF DateTime tag of the first directory with no offset, paired with the EXIF member of = models.DateSource; when neither gives one it MUST return modified unchanged with the FILE_MODIFIED member of = models.DateSource. It MUST NOT read the service clock.
judgement.why: The State 7 note passes only string-valued EXIF tags to the parser and treats every other representation, including bytes, as absent.

topics.topic: Calendar and time validity rules, including leap-second handling
questions: Which calendar and time rules define validity, particularly whether a matching value with a leap second such as second 60 is usable and, if so, how it is converted to a datetime?

quotes:
A camera value is unusable when it does not match the imported `EXIF_DATETIME_PATTERN` constant whole or is no valid calendar date and time, when its UTC year
   is before the imported `CAMERA_EARLIEST_YEAR` constant, or when it is more than the imported
   `CAMERA_LATEST_AFTER_MODIFIED_HOURS` constant of hours after the file's modification time.

4. The photo date is delivered as UTC without an offset, as the Client Portal stores it. A camera
   time with no offset is read in the time zone of that `timezone` field. A local time that occurs twice is the
   first occurrence, and a local time that does not exist is read with the offset in force before
   the clock change. A modification time is an absolute instant converted to UTC.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats second 60 as a valid leap second and normalizes it to the next UTC minute, while another treats it as an invalid calendar time and falls back to the next candidate photo moment; the calling flow and Portal observe different photo_date values and the placement can expose a different date_source.
judgement.why: The pattern admits second 60 syntactically, but neither State 2 nor the later note defines whether a leap second is a valid calendar time or how it becomes a datetime.

witness.initial: A decodable source has DateTimeOriginal `2016:12:31 23:59:60`, OffsetTimeOriginal `+00:00`, no usable DateTime value, and a usable modification time after that moment; the other plausibility limits pass.
events: The caller invokes delivery for the source photo.
The deliverer evaluates DateTimeOriginal as the first candidate for the photo moment.
outcomes: The deliverer accepts the leap second, normalizes it to `2017-01-01T00:00:00`, and uses the EXIF date source.
The deliverer rejects DateTimeOriginal as an invalid calendar time and uses the file modification time with the file-modified date source.
witness.observer: The calling flow and the Portal
basis:
The deliverer offers three operations: scan a project's folder, deliver one photo, and record its
publication.

3. The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then
   the file's modification time. `DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset matches
   the imported `EXIF_OFFSET_PATTERN` constant whole, with hours up to the imported `CAMERA_OFFSET_MAX_HOURS` constant and minutes up to 59; otherwise it is read in the time zone of the `timezone` field of the run settings (A8), and so is
   `DateTime`. A camera value is unusable when it does not match the imported `EXIF_DATETIME_PATTERN` constant whole or is no valid calendar date and time, when its UTC year
   is before the imported `CAMERA_EARLIEST_YEAR` constant, or when it is more than the imported
   `CAMERA_LATEST_AFTER_MODIFIED_HOURS` constant of hours after the file's modification time.

provenance.quote: The deliverer offers three operations: scan a project's folder, deliver one photo, and record its publication.
